newsitem.title: USA: Yachtsman sets sights on Pacific record.
newsitem.headline: Yachtsman sets sights on Pacific record.

text.p: An American yachtsman set sail on Wednesday with the dual aim of breaking the record for a solo Pacific Ocean crossing and of drawing attention to the capture of five killer whales in Japan.
Michael Reppy left Sausalito, near San Francisco, in his 36-foot (11-metre) trimaran "Nai'a", at the start of a planned solo voyage to Japan, spokeswoman Cindy Cione said.

Reppy, a 51-year-old physical therapist and environmentalist from Mill Valley, California, hopes to break the single-handed trans-Pacific sailing record which currently stands at 34 days, six hours and 26 minutes.

Reppy wants to draw attention to the capture in Taiji, Japan in February of five killer whales, or orcas. The killer whales have been sold to Japanese marine parks and are in poor health, according to a statement from environmentalists backing Reppy.
Reppy also wants to call attention to Japanese drive fishery, where whales and dolphins are herded into shallows and killed or sold to marine parks, the statement said.
